In a few weeks the standalone Hulu app will officially be no more

Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents:
Try something different:

The Walt Disney Company is nearing completion of a major new streaming plan. After several months, Disney executives said the company will finish merging Disney+ and Hulu into a single app this December, Variety reported. This will give subscribers access to all Disney+ and Hulu content in one place, along with other streaming perks.

Add Pocket-lint on Google Add as Preferred Source

Starting next month, Disney+ and Hulu bundle subscribers “will have a fully unified experience on Disney+, including live TV and select premium add-ons, creating a more seamless way to discover and engage with the breadth of content across our brands and franchise," Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston said in a letter to shareholders. “We believe our continued focus on product and technology will yield further benefits in engagement and churn over time.”

This merger has been years in the making, with Disney+ beginning its fusion with Hulu on December 6, 2023. At the time, the platform launched a beta version of the "Disney+ on Hulu" hub. The hub was fully integrated into the service in March 2024.

The merger comes after Disney experienced a sharp spike in revenue. According to Disney's letter to shareholders, during the fiscal fourth quarter ending on Oct. 3, the entertainment giant's streaming revenue rose by 19% to $6.1 billion, a billion dollars more than the previous year's fourth fiscal quarter. At the same time, subscription revenue grew by 22%.

"We are encouraged by our continued strong SVOD revenue growth and plan to invest behind this success. In fiscal 2027 we expect to increase both content and marketing investment in support of our longer-term goals," D'Amaro and Johnston said.

What other changes are coming to Disney+?

Expect creator content, free channels, and more

The merger is one of several major changes coming to Disney's flagship streaming service. Disney+ is planning to offer free channels to non-subscribers, giving them 24/7 access to ad-supported content, similar to Pluto TV, Tubi, and The Roku Channel. Additionally, Disney will add creator content to the platform under its agreement with TikTok. This new content rollout will be "strategically aligned" with the lead-up to the theatrical release of Avengers: Doomsday.

“We are also adding more vertical video, live sports and podcasts to the [Disney+] platform, while continuing to explore other emerging content genres,” D’Amaro and Johnston said.

These updates come after another spike in streaming prices for Disney+. In September, Disney announced higher prices aimed at encouraging people to purchase bundles. The Disney+/Hulu Premium bundle increased by $2 to $21.99/month. Also, Disney recently increased the amount of sports content available to Disney+ subscribers without an ESPN subscription, and it will play a key part in the platform's success in the near future.

"ESPN plays an important role in the overall Disney portfolio by contributing live and on-demand offerings to Disney+, lifting engagement and supporting revenue growth, and encouraging users to upgrade to the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Bundle," D’Amaro and Johnston said. "This fall, we increased the volume of sports content we offer Disney+ subscribers without the need for an ESPN subscription, continuing our simulcast of College GameDay, adding more live college football games, and airing select NFL games, which kicked off with the Dallas Cowboys at the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26."

How can I start streaming Disney+?

Why wait for the merger to start watching?

You can subscribe to Disney+ by going to the official website in your browser and selecting your preferred streaming plan. The cheapest bundle right now, which includes Disney+ and Hulu with ads, costs $12.99 per month. You can use the Disney+ app on OS or Android devices. The app is also accessible on smart TVs and streaming devices, such as Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire TV, and Chromecast.
